service.description:
Apply a DeviceConfig to a Device.
This service materializes the declared configuration values of a DeviceConfig onto an existing Device. It copies compatible DeviceConfig-level fields to the target Device and updates only existing device-bound Parameter rows that match source configuration parameters by parameterDefId and parameterAlias.
The service does not create ParameterDef rows, does not create missing Parameter(deviceId) rows, and does not write to the real physical device. It updates only Moqui-side Device and Parameter state.

Renders the recipe of a DeviceRuleSet as text files, one per DeviceRule priority, named ruleSetName_pNN.txt. Each line is name:=value, sorted by name.
Parameter lines: the Parameter records of the DeviceConfig of each DeviceRule. The name is the requestItemName of a DeviceRequestItem of the Parameter when there is one; otherwise it depends on DeviceConfig.deviceTypeEnumId: DtPLC gives dev.alias, DtMoquiPlc* gives dev.deviceName.alias, any other type gives the alias, or deviceName.parameterName. The alias is Parameter.parameterAlias, or ParameterDef.parameterName; deviceName is PhysicalDevice.deviceName, or the deviceId of the rule. The value is numericValue, else parameterEnumId, else symbolicValue.
Trajectory lines, when the DeviceConfig has an approximatedFunctionId: Trajectory.trajectoryId, Trajectory.pointCount and, for each TrajectoryPoint (index sequenceNum - 1), Trajectory.points[i].pos.v[d] (VectorComponent.realValue), .sequenceNum, .timeOffsetMs, .isBreakPoint, .hasBlendingOverride, .bufferMode and .transitionMode (from blendingEnumId), .blendingMode (ParametricPathPoint.tolerance).

service.description: Store logical samples of declared request items. Only DrpLogging creates ParameterLog; a missing purpose updates current Parameter values, writing only the last value of each parameter. Samples are written in chunks of 1000, one transaction each: the reads first, then the writes sent together, as a data load does. Results preserve input order; malformed or out-of-scope rows do not suppress later valid rows. When a chunk fails and the database answers, its samples are stored one by one to isolate the failing row. When the database does not answer, retryable is true and nothing from retryFromIndex on is stored: the caller keeps those samples (an MQTT session keeps them unacknowledged in the broker) and sends them again. A log row with the device-stamped sourceTime, or the sequenceNum, of a row already stored is a duplicate, not an error: a broker redelivers what was stored but not yet acknowledged. Use after#DeviceSamples for failure-isolated after-store extensions.

parameter.name: samples
parameter.description: Maps: deviceId, parameterId, value, optional sourceTime and receivedTime (timestamps), quality, optional log sequenceNum. Numeric values remain decimals.

parameter.name: acquisitionErrors
parameter.description: Transport/decode errors reported without dropping valid samples.

parameter.name: notifyErrors
parameter.description: False when the continuous host supplies its rate-limited health notifier.

parameter.name: retryable
parameter.description: The database did not answer: the samples from retryFromIndex on were not stored and are to be sent again.

service.description: Store decoded diagnostic events: ParameterLog for an exact parameterId, otherwise DeviceLog. The device must be the request owner or an alive descendant in its explicit device group hierarchy. Optional logValueKind is numeric, enumeration or message. Events always create logs. This service performs no wire-format decoding and needs no driver installed.
Extension hook after a successful sample batch has committed. Attach SECAs here for local after-store callbacks. Hook errors are logged and isolated from the saved data and persistence health.

Reads the waypoints of a planned trajectory (ApproximatedFunctionSample in sequenceNum order, each with its VectorComponent values) and returns one value list per axis. Axis names follow the vector space of the ApproximatedFunction: X,Y,Z,A,B,C for EngTcpPose6Dof, J1..J6 otherwise; a dimension beyond the sixth is named D and its index. TrajectoryAxisBinding is not used: this is the planned waypoint stream as it is.

service.description:
Publishes a planned trajectory for immediate execution (the ephemeral path; a recipe exported with export#DeviceConfig is the persistent one). The axis values come from get#TrajectoryAxes and go out as one JSON message through run#DeviceRequest: the DeviceRequest is an MQTT write without items (requestTypeEnumId DrtWrite, runServiceName moqui.device.gateway.MqttServices.run#DeviceRequest, brokerUri the broker, query the topic that MqttParameterSub on the PLC subscribes to).
